title: Beyond cold control. A neuroscientific perspective on hot executive functions in gambling and gaming disorder
abstract: Research on executive functions (EFs) in behavioural addictions (BAs) has predominantly focused on the cold domain, whereas the hot domain has received comparatively limited attention. This theoretical contribution examines Gambling Disorder (GD) and Internet Gaming Disorder (IGD), arguing that the social dimension of hot EFs represents a major gap in current research and intervention approaches for BAs. We discuss the strengths and limitations of existing interventions and highlight the need for a more socially grounded perspective. Furthermore, because traditional neuroscience paradigms often isolate individuals from their social environment—despite the central role of social interactions in hot EFs—we discuss the promise of socially situated decision-making scenarios and a hyperscanning approach as a possible answer to investigating the social dimension in this field of study. This perspective may provide a more ecologically valid assessment of EFs and inform the development of innovative neuroenhancement interventions for individuals with GD and IGD.
